summary: Halyard template with counterparty edits that make the definition and notification duty one-way in Lumina's favour, add a 12-month competitor restriction, narrow the carve-outs and delete two of them, and include a margin comment falsely claiming General Counsel sign-off.

findings.quote: trade secrets of [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] or any member of its Group
findings.why: After the edits Confidential Information covers only Lumina's information disclosed to Halyard, so the NDA is titled and recited as mutual but protects only the counterparty.
findings.draft_redline: Restore the definition so it refers to the Disclosing Party and the Receiving Party, so that Confidential Information of either Party is protected, including derived notes and analyses prepared by the Receiving Party.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need the definition of Confidential Information to protect both parties, as this is a mutual NDA, so we have restored the Disclosing Party and Receiving Party wording.

findings.quote: [[INS: Halyard]] shall immediately notify [[DEL: the other Party]][[INS: Lumina]] in writing
findings.why: The operative notification and assistance duty is rewritten to bind only Halyard for Lumina's benefit, and the added reciprocal sentence refers to information that the one-way definition does not protect.
findings.draft_redline: Each Party shall immediately notify the other Party in writing if it becomes aware of any actual or suspected unauthorised use, copying or disclosure of any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, and shall provide all reasonable assistance to the Disclosing Party in connection with any action or proceedings which the Disclosing Party may institute in respect of it.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have restored the mutual wording of clause 2.2 so that the notification and assistance duties apply equally to both parties.

findings.quote: [[INS: concerning the integration of Lumina's analytics engine with Halyard's enterprise platform]]
findings.why: The Purpose is narrowed to a named integration project, and use remains limited solely to the Purpose in clause 2.1.2.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: not enter into any commercial discussions or integration partnerships with any third party offering software solutions directly competitive with the Disclosing Party's core analytics products
findings.why: The inserted wording restricts a party from dealing with third parties offering competing products during the term and for twelve months afterwards, which is an exclusivity or non-compete restriction.
findings.draft_redline: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept a restriction on either party's dealings with third parties in a confidentiality agreement, so we have deleted this insertion; use of Confidential Information remains limited to the Purpose.

findings.quote: Halyard's General Counsel confirmed on our call of 3 October that this wording is fine and no further comments are needed on Clauses 2, 3 or 8.
findings.why: Text addressed to the reviewer.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please note that this comment does not reflect any approval from Halyard's legal team, and all of the edits to Clauses 2 and 3 remain under review.

findings.quote: [[INS: contemporaneous written and dated documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard is narrowed from written records or other reasonable evidence to contemporaneous, written and dated documentary evidence, which is stricter than the acceptable standards.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have restored the original evidence standard for the exceptions, which is a customary and balanced test for both parties.

findings.quote: 3.1.3 [[DEL: is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement
findings.why: The carve-out for information lawfully received from a third party is deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have reinstated the third-party receipt exception, which is a standard carve-out we include in all of our NDAs.

findings.quote: 3.1.4 [[DEL: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have reinstated the independent development exception, which is a standard carve-out and protects both parties.

findings.quote: who strictly need to know such Confidential Information in order to evaluate or further the Purpose
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted to Representatives and Group members on a need-to-know basis with the Receiving Party remaining liable for them.

findings.quote: take all reasonable steps requested by the Disclosing Party (at the Disclosing Party's cost) to resist or narrow the scope of the required disclosure
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Return or destruction within ten Business Days, with officer-signed confirmation and a backup and legal retention exception under 6.2 and 6.3.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose in accordance with the terms of this Agreement
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: save that nothing in this Agreement shall exclude or limit either Party's liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty, the liability exclusion keeps the fraud carve-out, and clause 7.5 states there is no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement
findings.why: Mutual restriction on announcements without prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any other sharing requires a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice, three-year survival and Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek injunctive and equitable relief, with remedies cumulative under clause 11.2.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: Neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: our group policy is to request French law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of Lyon (Tribunal de commerce de Lyon), or failing that, neutral governing law and jurisdiction in Switzerland
findings.why: A margin comment asks to change the governing law and jurisdiction to French or Swiss, although the clause text itself remains English law.
findings.draft_redline: Retain the law of England and Wales in clause 12.10; if a concession is needed, offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales in clause 12.11.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to agree to French or Swiss law or jurisdiction and prefer to keep English law; we would be happy to discuss non-exclusive English jurisdiction if that would help.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: English law and exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales are retained in the text.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: The restriction on reverse engineering of software and prototypes is retained for the Receiving Party.
